subject: Request: Launch-week QPS elevation + reconciliation credits
messages:
From: Alex Li <alex@launchloop.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: urgent QPS lift for launch week (June 9-12)

Kimberly —

We’re going live with LaunchLoop 2.0 next Wednesday and we just got the final traffic projection: peak bot traffic is ~3.2x our normal peak. We need a temporary throughput elevation (QPS and concurrency) from Redwood for 9–12 June to avoid user-facing errors.

Can you approve a provisional uplift (around 3x our current quota) with a clear reconciliation plan? We anticipate the extra consumption will be about 450k additional tokens across the window.

We can provide a PO and payment on receipt of a short-term amendment — but we’re asking for a small catch-up credit because some of the spike is due to a campaign Redwood helped promote.

Attached: launch_metrics.csv (sample telemetry + expected peak).

Thanks,
Alex Li
Head of Product
LaunchLoop

---
Attachment: launch_metrics.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex@launchloop.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: urgent QPS lift for launch week (June 9-12)

Alex —

Thanks for the heads-up and the CSV. Congrats on the launch. We can accommodate a provisional uplift, but we need to lock down three things quickly: (1) exact uplift numbers (QPS/concurrency), (2) PO or billing commitment window, and (3) reconciliation terms (how to true-up and size any credits).

Proposed short path from Redwood:
- Immediate provisional uplift to 3x current quota for 9–12 Jun (auto-revert on 13 Jun).
- Bill measured overrun at standard overage rate, then apply a one-time goodwill credit equal to 20% of overrun charges if LaunchLoop signs a 6-month commit by Jun 30.
- If you prefer, we can instead offer a fixed $X credit in lieu of the % — we’ll ask Ben to sketch the numbers.

Ben/Markus — can you draft the provisional pricing (expected token lift ~450k) and a PO template we can accept before Monday EOD? Alex, if procurement can send a signed provisional_PO-LaunchLoop-0610.pdf, we can fast-track the uplift.

Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

---
Attachment referenced: provisional_PO-LaunchLoop-0610.pdf (placeholder)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Li <alex@launchloop.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: urgent QPS lift for launch week (June 9-12) — pricing sketch

Following up with a quick sketch. Based on the 450k additional tokens and the customer’s current rate card, two options:

A) Pay-as-you-go with goodwill: bill overrun at standard overage ($0.015/token) => ~$6,750; issue 20% catch-up credit => credit $1,350; net uplift charge ~$5,400. Requires 6-month commit signed by Jun 30 to qualify for credit.

B) Short-term fixed uplift: flat launch-week uplift fee of $4,500 capped (prepaid); no additional overrun billing; no extra commit required but no later credit.

Operational notes: we’ll need a provisional PO by EOD Mon (6/7) to guarantee the capacity on our fleet. I’ll coordinate with ops to pin the uplift to a specific capacity pool so other customers aren’t impacted.

Markus — legal might want a one-paragraph amendment for auto-reversion and invoice reconciliation. Alex — which option do you prefer?

Ben Carter
Account Director, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Alex Li <alex@launchloop.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 07:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: urgent QPS lift for launch week (June 9-12) — pricing sketch

Ben / Kimberly —

Thanks, Ben. Option B (flat uplift fee $4,500 prepaid) is easier for procurement to sign against immediately. Please proceed with the provisional PO template and we’ll return it signed tonight. We still want the 20% credit path evaluated if we convert to a 6-month commit after launch, but for immediate execution we’ll do the fixed uplift.

One ask: can Redwood confirm that the uplift will be pinned to a separate capacity pool and that any throttling fallback on our primary pool would not route to degraded models? We want the uplift to be safe for user experience.

I’ll send procurement the signed provisional_PO-LaunchLoop-0610.pdf shortly.

—Alex

Alex —

We received the signed provisional PO (provisional_PO-LaunchLoop-0610.pdf). Ops has pinned a temporary capacity lane for LaunchLoop and set an auto-revert schedule for 2027-06-13 00:00 UTC. There is no degraded-model fallback for pinned lanes during the uplift window — we’ll keep your requests on the same model family you currently use.

Accounting will invoice the fixed uplift fee ($4,500) net 30; PO ref: LL-PO-0610. I’ve attached the amendment we used for similar short-term uplifts (one paragraph: auto-revert + reconciliation mechanics). If you later convert to a 6-month commit we’ll apply the 20% catch-up credit retroactively as discussed — Ben, please capture that condition in the HubSpot deal.

Markus Klein
